correctness.rationale: Common strict women-side priorities force serial dictatorship uniquely on both original and perturbed stable marriage. For any baseline available set R of cardinality k>=2, top two R elements of a random complete list are adjacent with probability k/n, and the uniformly chosen adjacent swap hits them with independent conditional probability 1/(n-1). Consequently stage-i pivotal events have constant conditional Bernoulli parameter k/[n(n-1)] and are mutually independent, even though R depends on earlier choices. By the first-differing stage, all pivots zero iff the entire stable matching survives. Therefore exact product PGF, Poisson-binomial law, lambda_n=(n+2)/(2n), Le Cam O(1/n), and log-Q_n=-1/2-7/(6n)+O(n^-2) follow. Independently enumerated all n=2,3 profiles and swaps and their pivot histograms, plus identities for n<=70. The n=4 archived checker is not treated as a proof of all n.
residual_risks: The theorem critically requires identical strict priorities, independent uniform complete proposer lists and exactly one independent adjacent swap per man; arbitrary multi-swap or correlated markets are not covered.

Resultary returned only the same November 8 record for the exact full-market Poisson-binomial product, and related one-agent-swap work cannot entail n simultaneous independent changes. Residual unindexed random serial-dictatorship sensitivity formulas are possible.
